texts.jdg.9.48: and Abimelech goeth up to mount Zalmon, he and all the people who [are] with him, and Abimelech taketh the great axe in his hand, and cutteth off a bough of the trees, and lifteth it up, and setteth [it] on his shoulder, and saith unto the people who [are] with him, `What ye have seen I have done -- haste, do ye like it.'
texts.jdg.9.49: And all the people also cut down each one his bough, and go after Abimelech, and set [them] at the high place, and burn by these the high place with fire, and also all the men of the tower of Shechem die, about a thousand men and women.
texts.jdg.9.50: And Abimelech goeth unto Thebez, and encampeth against Thebez, and captureth it,
texts.jdg.9.51: and a strong tower hath been in the midst of the city, and thither flee do all the men and the women, and all the masters of the city, and they shut [it] behind them, and go up on the roof of the tower.
texts.jdg.9.52: And Abimelech cometh unto the tower, and fighteth against it, and draweth nigh unto the opening of the tower to burn it with fire,
texts.jdg.9.53: and a certain woman doth cast a piece of a rider on the head of Abimelech, and breaketh his skull,
texts.jdg.9.54: and he calleth hastily unto the young man bearing his weapons, and saith to him, `Draw thy sword, and thou hast put me to death, lest they say of me -- A woman slew him;' and his young man pierced him through, and he dieth.
texts.jdg.9.55: And the men of Israel see that Abimelech [is] dead, and go each one to his place;
texts.jdg.9.56: and God turneth back the evil of Abimelech which he did to his father to slay his seventy brethren;
texts.jdg.9.57: and all the evil of the men of Shechem hath God turned back on their head, and come unto them doth the cursing of Jotham son of Jerubbaal.
texts.jdg.10.1: And there riseth after Abimelech, to save Israel, Tola son of Puah, son of Dodo, a man of Issachar, and he is dwelling in Shamir, in the hill-country of Ephraim,
texts.jdg.10.2: and he judgeth Israel twenty and three years, and he dieth, and is buried in Shamir.
texts.jdg.10.3: And there riseth after him Jair the Gileadite, and he judgeth Israel twenty and two years,
texts.jdg.10.4: and he hath thirty sons riding on thirty ass-colts, and they have thirty cities, (they call them Havoth-Jair unto this day), which [are] in the land of Gilead;
texts.jdg.10.5: and Jair dieth, and is buried in Kamon.
texts.jdg.10.6: And the sons of Israel add to do the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, and serve the Baalim, and Ashtaroth, and the gods of Aram, and the gods of Zidon, and the gods of Moab, and the gods of the Bene-Ammon, and the gods of the Philistines, and forsake Jehovah, and have not served Him;
texts.jdg.10.7: and the anger of Jehovah burneth against Israel, and He selleth them into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the Bene-Ammon,
texts.jdg.10.8: and they crush and oppress the sons of Israel in that year -- eighteen years all the sons of Israel [who] are beyond the Jordan, in the land of the Amorite, which [is] in Gilead.
texts.jdg.10.9: And the Bene-Ammon pass over the Jordan to fight also against Judah, and against Benjamin, and against the house of Ephraim, and Israel hath great distress.
texts.jdg.10.10: And the sons of Israel cry unto Jehovah, saying, `We have sinned against Thee, even because we have forsaken our God, and serve the Baalim.'
texts.jdg.10.11: And Jehovah saith unto the sons of Israel, `[Have I] not [saved you] from the Egyptians, and from the Amorite, from the Bene-Ammon, and from the Philistines?
texts.jdg.10.12: And the Zidonians, and Amalek, and Maon have oppressed you, and ye cry unto Me, and I save you out of their hand;
texts.jdg.10.13: and ye -- ye have forsaken Me, and serve other gods, therefore I add not to save you.
texts.jdg.10.14: Go and cry unto the gods on which ye have fixed; they -- they save you in the time of your adversity.'
texts.jdg.10.15: And the sons of Israel say unto Jehovah, `We have sinned, do Thou to us according to all that is good in Thine eyes; only deliver us, we pray Thee, this day.'
texts.jdg.10.16: And they turn aside the gods of the stranger out of their midst, and serve Jehovah, and His soul is grieved with the misery of Israel.
texts.jdg.10.17: And the Bene-Ammon are called together, and encamp in Gilead, and the sons of Israel are gathered together, and encamp in Mizpah.
texts.jdg.10.18: And the people -- heads of Gilead -- say one unto another, `Who [is] the man that doth begin to fight against the Bene-Ammon? he is for head to all inhabitants of Gilead.'
texts.jdg.11.1: And Jephthah the Gileadite hath been a mighty man of valour, and he [is] son of a woman, a harlot; and Gilead begetteth Jephthah,
texts.jdg.11.2: and the wife of Gilead beareth to him sons, and the wife's sons grow up and cast out Jephthah, and say to him, `Thou dost not inherit in the house of our father; for son of another woman [art] thou.'
texts.jdg.11.3: And Jephthah fleeth from the face of his brethren, and dwelleth in the land of Tob; and vain men gather themselves together unto Jephthah, and they go out with him.
texts.jdg.11.4: And it cometh to pass, after a time, that the Bene-Ammon fight with Israel,
texts.jdg.11.5: and it cometh to pass, when the Bene-Ammon have fought with Israel, that the elders of Gilead go to take Jephthah from the land of Tob;
texts.jdg.11.6: and they say unto Jephthah, `Come, and thou hast been to us for captain, and we fight against the Bene-Ammon.'
texts.jdg.11.7: And Jephthah saith to the elders of Gilead, `Have not ye hated me? and ye cast me out from the house of my father, and wherefore have ye come unto me now when ye are in distress?'
texts.jdg.11.8: and the elders of Gilead say unto Jephthah, `Therefore, now, we have turned back unto thee; and thou hast gone with us, and fought against the Bene-Ammon, and thou hast been to us for head -- to all the inhabitants of Gilead.'
texts.jdg.11.9: And Jephthah saith unto the elders of Gilead, `If ye are taking me back to fight against the Bene-Ammon, and Jehovah hath given them before me -- I, am I to you for a head?'
texts.jdg.11.10: And the elders of Gilead say unto Jephthah, `Jehovah is hearkening between us -- if according to thy word we do not so.'
texts.jdg.11.11: And Jephthah goeth with the elders of Gilead, and the people set him over them for head and for captain, and Jephthah speaketh all his words before Jehovah in Mizpeh.
texts.jdg.11.12: And Jephthah sendeth messengers unto the king of the Bene-Ammon, saying, `What -- to me and to thee, that thou hast come in unto me, to fight in my land.'
texts.jdg.11.13: And the king of the Bene-Ammon saith unto the messengers of Jephthah, `Because Israel took my land in his coming up out of Egypt, from Arnon, and unto the Jabbok, and unto the Jordan; and now, restore them in peace.'
texts.jdg.11.14: And Jephthah addeth yet and sendeth messengers unto the king of the Bene-Ammon,
texts.jdg.11.15: and saith to him, `Thus said Jephthah, Israel took not the land of Moab, and the land of the Bene-Ammon,
texts.jdg.11.16: for in their coming up out of Egypt, Israel goeth in the wilderness unto the Red Sea, and cometh in to Kadesh,
texts.jdg.11.17: and Israel sendeth messengers unto the king of Edom, saying, Let me pass over, I pray thee, through thy land, and the king of Edom hearkened not; and also unto the king of Moab hath [Israel] sent, and he hath not been willing; and Israel abideth in Kadesh,
texts.jdg.11.18: and he goeth through the wilderness, and compasseth the land of Edom and the land of Moab, and cometh in at the rising of the sun of the land of Moab, and they encamp beyond Arnon, and have not come into the border of Moab, for Arnon [is] the border of Moab.
texts.jdg.11.19: `And Israel sendeth messengers unto Sihon, king of the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and Israel saith to him, Let us pass over, we pray thee, through thy land, unto my place,
texts.jdg.11.20: and Sihon hath not trusted Israel to pass over through his border, and Sihon gathereth all his people, and they encamp in Jahaz, and fight with Israel;
texts.jdg.11.21: and Jehovah, God of Israel, giveth Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they smite them, and Israel possesseth all the land of the Amorite, the inhabitant of that land,
texts.jdg.11.22: and they possess all the border of the Amorite from Arnon, and unto the Jabbok, and from the wilderness, and unto the Jordan.
texts.jdg.11.23: `And now, Jehovah, God of Israel, hath dispossessed the Amorite from the presence of His people Israel, and thou wouldst possess it!
texts.jdg.11.24: That which Chemosh thy god causeth thee to possess -- dost thou not possess it? and all that which Jehovah our God hath dispossessed from our presence, -- it we do possess.
texts.jdg.11.25: `And now, [art] thou at all better than Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab? did he at all strive with Israel? did he at all fight against them?
texts.jdg.11.26: In Israel's dwelling in Heshbon and in its towns, and in Aroer and in its towns, and in all the cities which [are] by the sides of Arnon three hundred years -- and wherefore have ye not delivered them in that time?
texts.jdg.11.27: And I -- I have not sinned against thee, and thou art doing with me evil -- to fight against me. Jehovah, the Judge, doth judge to-day between the sons of Israel and the sons of Ammon.'
texts.jdg.11.28: And the king of the Bene-Ammon hath not hearkened unto the words of Jephthah which he sent unto him,
texts.jdg.11.29: and the Spirit of Jehovah is on Jephthah, and he passeth over Gilead and Manasseh, and passeth over Mizpeh of Gilead, and from Mizpeh of Gilead he hath passed over to the Bene-Ammon.
texts.jdg.11.30: And Jephthah voweth a vow to Jehovah, and saith, `If Thou dost at all give the Bene-Ammon into my hand --
texts.jdg.11.31: then it hath been, that which at all cometh out from the doors of my house to meet me in my turning back in peace from the Bene-Ammon -- it hath been to Jehovah, or I have offered up for it -- a burnt-offering.'
texts.jdg.11.32: And Jephthah passeth over unto the Bene-Ammon to fight against them, and Jehovah giveth them into his hand,
texts.jdg.11.33: and he smiteth them from Aroer, and unto thy going in to Minnith, twenty cities, and unto the meadow of the vineyards -- a very great smiting; and the Bene-Ammon are humbled at the presence of the sons of Israel.
texts.jdg.11.34: And Jephthah cometh into Mizpeh, unto his house, and lo, his daughter is coming out to meet him with timbrels, and with choruses, and save her alone, he hath none, son or daughter.
texts.jdg.11.35: And it cometh to pass, when he seeth her, that he rendeth his garments, and saith, `Alas, my daughter, thou hast caused me greatly to bend, and thou hast been among those troubling me; and I -- I have opened my mouth unto Jehovah, and I am not able to turn back.'
texts.jdg.11.36: And she saith unto him, `My father -- thou hast opened thy mouth unto Jehovah, do to me as it hath gone out from thy mouth, after that Jehovah hath done for thee vengeance on thine enemies, on the Bene-Ammon.'
texts.jdg.11.37: And she saith unto her father, `Let this thing be done to me; desist from me two months, and I go on, and have gone down on the hills, and I weep for my virginity -- I and my friends.'
texts.jdg.11.38: And he saith, `Go;' and he sendeth her away two months, and she goeth, she and her friends, and she weepeth for her virginity on the hills;
texts.jdg.11.39: and it cometh to pass at the end of two months that she turneth back unto her father, and he doth to her his vow which he hath vowed, and she knew not a man; and it is a statute in Israel:
texts.jdg.11.40: from time to time the daughters of Israel go to talk to the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite, four days in a year.
texts.jdg.12.1: And the men of Ephraim are called together, and pass over northward, and say to Jephthah, `Wherefore has thou passed over to fight against the Bene-Ammon, and on us hast not called to go with thee? thy house we burn over thee with fire.'
texts.jdg.12.2: And Jephthah saith unto them, `A man of great strife I have been (I and my people) with the Bene-Ammon, and I call you, and ye have not saved me out of their hand,
texts.jdg.12.3: and I see that thou art not a saviour, and I put my life in my hand, and pass over unto the Bene-Ammon, and Jehovah giveth them into my hand -- and why have ye come up unto me this day to fight against me?'
texts.jdg.12.4: And Jephthah gathered all the men of Gilead, and fighteth with Ephraim, and the men of Gilead smite Ephraim, because they said, `Fugitives of Ephraim [are] ye Gileadites, in the midst of Ephraim -- in the midst of Manasseh.'
texts.jdg.12.5: And Gilead captureth the passages of the Jordan to Ephraim, and it hath been, when [any of] the fugitives of Ephraim say, `Let me pass over,' and the men of Gilead say to him, `An Ephramite thou?' and he saith, `No;'
texts.jdg.12.6: that they say to him, `Say, I pray thee, Shibboleth;' and he saith, `Sibboleth,' and is not prepared to speak right -- and they seize him, and slaughter him at the passages of the Jordan, and there fall at that time, of Ephraim, forty and two chiefs.
texts.jdg.12.7: And Jephthah judged Israel six years, and Jephthah the Gileadite dieth, and is buried in [one of] the cities of Gilead.
texts.jdg.12.8: And after him Ibzan of Beth-Lehem judgeth Israel,
texts.jdg.12.9: and he hath thirty sons and thirty daughters, he hath sent without and thirty daughters hath brought in to his sons from without; and he judgeth Israel seven years.
texts.jdg.12.10: And Ibzan dieth, and is buried in Beth-Lehem.
texts.jdg.12.11: And after him Elon the Zebulunite judgeth Israel, and he judgeth Israel ten years,
texts.jdg.12.12: and Elon the Zebulunite dieth, and is buried in Aijalon, in the land of Zebulun.
texts.jdg.12.13: And after him, Abdon son of Hillel, the Pirathonite, judgeth Israel,
texts.jdg.12.14: and he hath forty sons, and thirty grandsons, riding on seventy ass-colts, and he judgeth Israel eight years.
texts.jdg.12.15: And Abdon son of Hillel, the Pirathonite, dieth, and is buried in Pirathon, in the land of Ephraim, in the hill-country of the Amalekite.
texts.jdg.13.1: And the sons of Israel add to do the evil thing in the eyes of Jehovah, and Jehovah giveth them into the hand of the Philistines forty years.
texts.jdg.13.2: And there is a certain man of Zorah, of the family of the Danite, and his name [is] Manoah, his wife [is] barren, and hath not borne;
texts.jdg.13.3: and a messenger of Jehovah appeareth unto the woman, and saith unto her, `Lo, I pray thee, thou [art] barren, and hast not borne; when thou hast conceived, then thou hast borne a son.
texts.jdg.13.4: And, now, take heed, I pray thee, and do not drink wine, and strong drink, and do not eat any unclean thing,
texts.jdg.13.5: for, lo, thou art conceiving and bearing a son, and a razor doth not go up on his head, for a Nazarite to God is the youth from the womb, and he doth begin to save Israel out of the hand of the Philistines.'
texts.jdg.13.6: And the woman cometh and speaketh to her husband, saying, `A man of God hath come unto me, and his appearance [is] as the appearance of a messenger of God, very fearful, and I have not asked him whence he [is], and his name he hath not declared to me;
texts.jdg.13.7: and he saith to me, Lo, thou art pregnant, and bearing a son, and now do not drink wine and strong drink, and do not eat any unclean thing, for a Nazarite to God is the youth from the womb till the day of his death.'
texts.jdg.13.8: And Manoah maketh entreaty unto Jehovah, and saith, `O, my Lord, the man of God whom Thou didst send, let him come in, I pray thee, again unto us, and direct us what we do to the youth who is born.'
texts.jdg.13.9: And God hearkeneth to the voice of Manoah, and the messenger of God cometh again unto the woman, and she [is] sitting in a field, and Manoah her husband is not with her,
texts.jdg.13.10: and the woman hasteth, and runneth, and declareth to her husband, and saith unto him, `Lo, he hath appeared unto me -- the man who came on [that] day unto me.'
texts.jdg.13.11: And Manoah riseth, and goeth after his wife, and cometh unto the man, and saith to him, `Art thou the man who spake unto the woman?' and he saith, `I [am].'
texts.jdg.13.12: And Manoah saith, `Now let thy words come to pass; what is the custom of the youth -- and his work?'
texts.jdg.13.13: And the messenger of Jehovah saith unto Manoah, `Of all that I said unto the woman let her take heed;
texts.jdg.13.14: of anything which cometh out from the wine-vine she doth not eat, and wine and strong drink she doth not drink, and any unclean thing she doth not eat; all that I have commanded her she doth observe.'
texts.jdg.13.15: And Manoah saith unto the messenger of Jehovah, `Let us detain thee, we pray thee, and prepare before thee a kid of the goats.'
texts.jdg.13.16: And the messenger of Jehovah saith unto Manoah, `If thou detain me -- I do not eat of thy bread; and if thou prepare a burnt-offering -- to Jehovah thou dost offer it;' for Manoah hath not known that He [is] a messenger of Jehovah.
texts.jdg.13.17: And Manoah saith unto the messenger of Jehovah, `What [is] thy name? when thy words come to pass, then we have honoured thee.'
texts.jdg.13.18: And the messenger of Jehovah saith to him, `Why [is] this -- thou dost ask for My name? -- and it [is] Wonderful.'
texts.jdg.13.19: And Manoah taketh the kid of the goats, and the present, and offereth on the rock to Jehovah, and He is doing wonderfully, and Manoah and his wife are looking on,
texts.jdg.13.20: and it cometh to pass, in the going up of the flame from off the altar toward the heavens, that the messenger of Jehovah goeth up in the flame of the altar, and Manoah and his wife are looking on, and they fall on their faces to the earth,
texts.jdg.13.21: and the messenger of Jehovah hath not added again to appear unto Manoah, and unto his wife, then hath Manoah known that He [is] a messenger of Jehovah.
texts.jdg.13.22: And Manoah saith unto his wife, `We certainly die, for we have seen God.'
texts.jdg.13.23: And his wife saith to him, `If Jehovah were desirous to put us to death, He had not received from our hands burnt-offering and present, nor shewed us all these things, nor as [at this] time caused us to hear [anything] like this.'
texts.jdg.13.24: And the woman beareth a son, and calleth his name Samson, and the youth groweth, and Jehovah doth bless him,
texts.jdg.13.25: and the Spirit of Jehovah beginneth to move him in the camp of Dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.
texts.jdg.14.1: And Samson goeth down to Timnath, and seeth a woman in Timnath of the daughters of the Philistines,
texts.jdg.14.2: and cometh up and declareth to his father, and to his mother, and saith, `A woman I have seen in Timnath, of the daughters of the Philistines; and now, take her for me for a wife.'
texts.jdg.14.3: And his father saith to him -- also his mother, `Is there not among the daughters of thy brethren, and among all my people, a woman, that thou art going to take a woman from the uncircumcised Philistines?' and Samson saith unto his father, `Take her for me, for she is right in mine eyes.'
texts.jdg.14.4: And his father and his mother have not known that from Jehovah it [is], that a meeting he is seeking of the Philistines; and at that time the Philistines are ruling over Israel.
texts.jdg.14.5: And Samson goeth down -- also his father and his mother, to Timnath, and they come unto the vineyards of Timnath, and lo, a lion's whelp roareth at meeting him,
texts.jdg.14.6: and the Spirit of Jehovah prospereth over him, and he rendeth it as the rending of a kid, and there is nothing in his hand, and he hath not declared to his father and to his mother that which he hath done.
texts.jdg.14.7: And he goeth down and speaketh to the woman, and she is right in the eyes of Samson;
texts.jdg.14.8: and he turneth back after [some] days to take her, and turneth aside to see the carcase of the lion, and lo, a company of bees [are] in the body of the lion -- and honey.
texts.jdg.14.9: And he taketh it down on to his hands, and goeth on, going and eating; and he goeth unto his father, and unto his mother, and giveth to them, and they eat, and he hath not declared to them that from the body of the lion he took down the honey.
texts.jdg.14.10: And his father goeth down unto the woman, and Samson maketh there a banquet, for so the young men do;
texts.jdg.14.11: and it cometh to pass when they see him, that they take thirty companions, and they are with him.
texts.jdg.14.12: And Samson saith to them, `Let me, I pray you, put forth to you a riddle; if ye certainly declare it to me [in] the seven days of the banquet, and have found [it] out, then I have given to you thirty linen shirts, and thirty changes of garments;
texts.jdg.14.13: and if ye are not able to declare [it] to me, then ye have given to me thirty linen shirts, and thirty changes of garments.' And they say to him, `Put forth thy riddle, and we hear it!'
texts.jdg.14.14: And he saith to them: `Out of the eater came forth meat, And out of the strong came forth sweetness;' and they were not able to declare the riddle [in] three days.
texts.jdg.14.15: And it cometh to pass, on the seventh day, that they say to Samson's wife, `Entice thy husband, that he declare to us the riddle, lest we burn thee and the house of thy father with fire; to possess us have ye called for us? is it not?'
texts.jdg.14.16: And Samson's wife weepeth for it, and saith, `Thou hast only hated me, and hast not loved me; the riddle thou hast put forth to the sons of my people -- and to me thou hast not declared it;' and he saith to her, `Lo, to my father and to my mother I have not declared [it] -- and to thee I declare [it]!'
texts.jdg.14.17: And she weepeth for it the seven days [in] which their banquet hath been, and it cometh to pass on the seventh day that he declareth [it] to her, for she hath distressed him; and she declareth the riddle to the sons of her people.
texts.jdg.14.18: And the men of the city say to him on the seventh day, before the sun goeth in: -- `What [is] sweeter than honey? And what stronger than a lion?' And he saith to them: `Unless ye had ploughed with my heifer, Ye had not found out my riddle.'
texts.jdg.14.19: And the Spirit of Jehovah prospereth over him, and he goeth down to Ashkelon, and smiteth of them thirty men, and taketh their armour, and giveth the changes to those declaring the riddle; and his anger burneth, and he goeth up to the house of his father;
texts.jdg.14.20: and Samson's wife becometh his companion's, who [is] his friend.
texts.jdg.15.1: And it cometh to pass, after [some] days, in the days of wheat-harvest, that Samson looketh after his wife, with a kid of the goats, and saith, `I go in unto my wife, to the inner chamber;' and her father hath not permitted him to go in,
texts.jdg.15.2: and her father saith, I certainly said, that thou didst certainly hate her, and I give her to thy companion; is not her sister -- the young one -- better than she? Let her be, I pray thee, to thee, instead of her.'
texts.jdg.15.3: And Samson saith of them, `I am more innocent this time than the Philistines, though I am doing with them evil.'
texts.jdg.15.4: And Samson goeth and catcheth three hundred foxes, and taketh torches, and turneth tail unto tail, and putteth a torch between the two tails, in the midst,
texts.jdg.15.5: and kindleth fire in the torches, and sendeth [them] out into the standing corn of the Philistines, and burneth [it] from heap even unto standing corn, even unto vineyard -- olive-yard.
texts.jdg.15.6: And the Philistines say, `Who hath done this?' And they say, `Samson, son-in-law of the Timnite, because he hath taken away his wife, and giveth her to his companion;' and the Philistines go up, and burn her and her father with fire.
texts.jdg.15.7: And Samson saith to them, `Though ye do thus, nevertheless I am avenged on you, and afterwards I cease!'
texts.jdg.15.8: And he smiteth them hip and thigh -- a great smiting, and goeth down and dwelleth in the cleft of the rock Etam.
texts.jdg.15.9: And the Philistines go up, and encamp in Judah, and are spread out in Lehi,
texts.jdg.15.10: and the men of Judah say, `Why have ye come up against us?' and they say, `To bind Samson we have come up, to do to him as he hath done to us.'
texts.jdg.15.11: And three thousand men of Judah go down unto the cleft of the rock Etam, and say to Samson, `Hast thou now known that the Philistines are rulers over us? and what [is] this thou hast done to us?' And he saith to them, `As they did to me, so I did to them.'
texts.jdg.15.12: And they say to him, `To bind thee we have come down -- to give thee into the hand of the Philistines.' And Samson saith to them, `Swear to me, lest ye fall upon me yourselves.'
texts.jdg.15.13: And they speak to him, saying, No, but we certainly bind thee, and have given thee into their hand, and we certainly do not put thee to death;' and they bind him with two thick bands, new ones, and bring him up from the rock.
texts.jdg.15.14: He hath come unto Lehi -- and the Philistines have shouted at meeting him -- and the Spirit of Jehovah prospereth over him, and the thick bands which [are] on his arms are as flax which they burn with fire, and his bands are wasted from off his hands,
texts.jdg.15.15: and he findeth a fresh jaw-bone of an ass, and putteth forth his hand and taketh it, and smiteth with it -- a thousand men.
texts.jdg.15.16: And Samson saith, `With a jaw-bone of the ass -- an ass upon asses -- with a jaw-bone of the ass I have smitten a thousand men.'
texts.jdg.15.17: And it cometh to pass when he finisheth speaking, that he casteth away the jaw-bone out of his hand, and calleth that place Ramath-Lehi;
texts.jdg.15.18: and he thirsteth exceedingly, and calleth unto Jehovah, and saith, `Thou -- Thou hast given by the hand of Thy servant this great salvation; and now, I die with thirst, and have fallen into the hand of the uncircumcised.'
texts.jdg.15.19: And God cleaveth the hollow place which [is] in Lehi, and waters come out of it, and he drinketh, and his spirit cometh back, and he reviveth; therefore hath [one] called its name `The fountain of him who is calling,' which [is] in Lehi unto this day.
texts.jdg.15.20: And he judgeth Israel in the days of the Philistines twenty years.
texts.jdg.16.1: And Samson goeth to Gaza, and seeth there a woman, a harlot, and goeth in unto her;
texts.jdg.16.2: [it is told] to the Gazathites, saying, `Samson hath come in hither;' and they go round and lay wait for him all the night at the gate of the city, and keep themselves silent all the night, saying, `Till the light of the morning -- then we have slain him.'
texts.jdg.16.3: And Samson lieth down till the middle of the night, and riseth in the middle of the night, and layeth hold on the doors of the gate of the city, and on the two side posts, and removeth them with the bar, and putteth on his shoulders, and taketh them up unto the top of the hill, which [is] on the front of Hebron.
texts.jdg.16.4: And it cometh to pass afterwards that he loveth a woman in the valley of Sorek, and her name [is] Delilah,
texts.jdg.16.5: and the princes of the Philistines come up unto her, and say to her, `Entice him, and see wherein his great power [is], and wherein we are able for him -- and we have bound him to afflict him, and we -- we give to thee, each one, eleven hundred silverlings.'
texts.jdg.16.6: And Delilah saith unto Samson, `Declare, I pray thee, to me, wherein thy great power [is], and wherewith thou art bound, to afflict thee.'
texts.jdg.16.7: And Samson saith unto her, `If they bind me with seven green withs which have not been dried, then I have been weak, and have been as one of the human race.'
texts.jdg.16.8: And the princes of the Philistines bring up to her seven green withs which have not been dried, and she bindeth him with them.
texts.jdg.16.9: And the ambush is abiding with her in an inner chamber, and she saith unto him, `Philistines [are] upon thee, Samson;' and he breaketh the withs as a thread of tow is broken in its smelling fire, and his power hath not been known.
texts.jdg.16.10: And Delilah saith unto Samson, `Lo, thou hast played upon me, and speakest unto me lies; now, declare, I pray thee, to me, wherewith thou art bound.'
texts.jdg.16.11: And he saith unto her, `If they certainly bind me with thick bands, new ones, by which work hath not been done, then I have been weak, and have been as one of the human race.'
texts.jdg.16.12: And Delilah taketh thick bands, new ones, and bindeth him with them, and saith unto him, `Philistines [are] upon thee, Samson;' and the ambush is abiding in an inner chamber, and he breaketh them from off his arms as a thread.
texts.jdg.16.13: And Delilah saith unto Samson, `Hitherto thou hast played upon me, and dost speak unto me lies; declare to me wherewith thou art bound.' And he saith unto her, `If thou weavest the seven locks of my head with the web.'
texts.jdg.16.14: And she fixeth [it] with the pin, and saith unto him, `Philistines [are] upon thee, Samson;' and he awaketh out of his sleep, and journeyeth with the pin of the weaving machine, and with the web.
texts.jdg.16.15: And she saith unto him, `How dost thou say, I have loved thee, and thy heart is not with me? these three times thou hast played upon me, and hast not declared to me wherein thy great power [is].'
texts.jdg.16.16: And it cometh to pass, because she distressed him with her words all the days, and doth urge him, and his soul is grieved to death,
texts.jdg.16.17: that he declareth to her all his heart, and saith to her, `A razor hath not gone up on my head, for a Nazarite to God I [am] from the womb of my mother; if I have been shaven, then hath my power turned aside from me, and I have been weak, and have been as any of the human race.'
texts.jdg.16.18: And Delilah seeth that he hath declared to her all his heart, and she sendeth and calleth for the princes of the Philistines, saying, `Come up this time, for he hath declared to me all his heart;' and the princes of the Philistines have come up unto her, and bring up the money in their hand.
texts.jdg.16.19: and she maketh him sleep on her knees, and calleth for a man, and shaveth the seven locks of his head, and beginneth to afflict him, and his power turneth aside from off him;
texts.jdg.16.20: and she saith, `Philistines [are] upon thee, Samson;' and he awaketh out of his sleep, and saith, `I go out as time by time, and shake myself;' and he hath not known that Jehovah hath turned aside from off him.
texts.jdg.16.21: And the Philistines seize him, and pick out his eyes, and bring him down to Gaza, and bind him with two brazen fetters; and he is grinding in the prison-house.
texts.jdg.16.22: And the hair of his head beginneth to shoot up, when he hath been shaven,
texts.jdg.16.23: and the princes of the Philistines have been gathered together to sacrifice a great sacrifice to Dagon their god, and to rejoice; and they say, `Our god hath given into our hand Samson our enemy.'
texts.jdg.16.24: And the people see him, and praise their god, for they said, `Our god hath given in our hand our enemy, and he who is laying waste our land, and who multiplied our wounded.'
texts.jdg.16.25: And it cometh to pass, when their heart [is] glad, that they say, `Call for Samson, and he doth play before us;' and they call for Samson out of the prison-house, and he playeth before them, and they cause him to stand between the pillars.
texts.jdg.16.26: And Samson saith unto the young man who is keeping hold on his hand, `Let me alone, and let me feel the pillars on which the house is established, and I lean upon them.'
texts.jdg.16.27: And the house hath been full of men and of women, and thither [are] all the princes of the Philistines, and on the roof [are] about three thousand men and women, who are looking on the playing of Samson.
texts.jdg.16.28: And Samson calleth unto Jehovah, and saith, `Lord Jehovah, remember me, I pray Thee, and strengthen me, I pray Thee, only this time, O God; and I am avenged -- vengeance at once -- because of my two eyes, on the Philistines.'
texts.jdg.16.29: And Samson turneth aside [to] the two middle pillars, on which the house is established, and on which it is supported, [to] the one with his right hand, and one with his left;
texts.jdg.16.30: and Samson saith, `Let me die with the Philistines,' and he inclineth himself powerfully, and the house falleth on the princes, and on all the people who [are] in it, and the dead whom he hath put to death in his death are more than those whom he put to death in his life.
texts.jdg.16.31: And his brethren come down, and all the house of his father, and lift him up, and bring him up, and bury him between Zorah and Eshtaol, in the burying-place of Manoah his father; and he hath judged Israel twenty years.
texts.jdg.17.1: And there is a man of the hill-country of Ephraim, and his name [is] Micah,
texts.jdg.17.2: and he saith to his mother, `The eleven hundred silverlings which have been taken of thine, and [of which] thou hast sworn, and also spoken in mine ears; lo, the silver [is] with me, I have taken it;' and his mother saith, `Blessed [is] my son of Jehovah.'
texts.jdg.17.3: And he giveth back the eleven hundred silverlings to his mother, and his mother saith, `I had certainly sanctified the silver to Jehovah, from my hand, for my son, to make a graven image, and a molten image; and now, I give it back to thee.'
texts.jdg.17.4: And he giveth back the money to his mother, and his mother taketh two hundred silverlings, and giveth them to a refiner, and he maketh them a graven image, and a molten image, and it is in the house of Micah.
texts.jdg.17.5: As to the man Micah, he hath a house of gods, and he maketh an ephod, and teraphim, and consecrateth the hand of one of his sons, and he is to him for a priest;
texts.jdg.17.6: in those days there is no king in Israel, each that which is right in his own eyes doth.
texts.jdg.17.7: And there is a young man of Beth-Lehem-Judah, of the family of Judah, and he [is] a Levite, and he [is] a sojourner there.
texts.jdg.17.8: And the man goeth out of the city, out of Beth-Lehem-Judah, to sojourn where he doth find, and cometh to the hill-country of Ephraim, unto the house of Micah, to work his way.
texts.jdg.17.9: And Micah saith to him, `Whence comest thou?' and he saith unto him, `A Levite [am] I, of Beth-Lehem-Judah, and I am going to sojourn where I do find.'
texts.jdg.17.10: And Micah saith to him, `Dwell with me, and be to me for a father and for a priest, and I give to thee ten silverlings for the days, and a suit of garments, and thy sustenance;' and the Levite goeth [in].
texts.jdg.17.11: And the Levite is willing to dwell with the man, and the young man is to him as one of his sons.
texts.jdg.17.12: And Micah consecrateth the hand of the Levite, and the young man is to him for a priest, and he is in the house of Micah,
texts.jdg.17.13: and Micah saith, `Now I have known that Jehovah doth good to me, for the Levite hath been to me for a priest.'
texts.jdg.18.1: In those days there is no king in Israel, and in those days the tribe of the Danite is seeking for itself an inheritance to inhabit, for [that] hath not fallen to it unto that day in the midst of the tribes of Israel by inheritance.
texts.jdg.18.2: And the sons of Dan send, out of their family, five men of them, men, sons of valour, from Zorah, and from Eshtaol, to traverse the land, and to search it, and they say unto them, `Go, search the land;' and they come into the hill-country of Ephraim, unto the house of Micah, and lodge there.
texts.jdg.18.3: They [are] with the household of Micah, and they have discerned the voice of the young man, the Levite, and turn aside there, and say to him, `Who hath brought thee hither? and what art thou doing in this [place?] and what to thee here?'
texts.jdg.18.4: And he saith unto them, `Thus and thus hath Micah done to me; and he hireth me, and I am to him for a priest.'
texts.jdg.18.5: And they say to him, `Ask, we pray thee, at God, and we know whether our way is prosperous on which we are going.'
texts.jdg.18.6: And the priest saith to them, `Go in peace; over-against Jehovah [is] your way in which ye go.'
texts.jdg.18.7: And the five men go, and come in to Laish, and see the people which [is] in its midst, dwelling confidently, according to the custom of Zidonians, quiet and confident; and there is none putting to shame in the land in [any] thing, possessing restraint, and they [are] far off from the Zidonians, and have no word with [any] man.
texts.jdg.18.8: And they come in unto their brethren, at Zorah and Eshtaol, and their brethren say to them, `What -- ye?'
texts.jdg.18.9: And they say, `Rise, and we go up against them, for we have seen the land, and lo, very good; and ye are keeping silent! be not slothful to go -- to enter to possess the land.
texts.jdg.18.10: When ye go, ye come in unto a people confident, and the land [is] large on both hands, for God hath given it into your hand, a place where there is no lack of anything which [is] in the land.'
texts.jdg.18.11: And there journey thence, of the family of the Danite, from Zorah, and from Eshtaol, six hundred men girded with weapons of war.
texts.jdg.18.12: And they go up and encamp in Kirjath-Jearim, in Judah, therefore they have called that place, `Camp of Dan,' till this day; lo, behind Kirjath-Jearim.
texts.jdg.18.13: And they pass over thence [to] the hill-country of Ephraim, and come in unto the house of Micah.
texts.jdg.18.14: And the five men, those going to traverse the land of Laish, answer and say unto their brethren, `Have ye known that there is in these houses an ephod, and teraphim, and graven image, and molten image? and now, know what ye do.'
texts.jdg.18.15: And they turn aside thither, and come in unto the house of the young man the Levite, the house of Micah, and ask of him of welfare, --
texts.jdg.18.16: (and the six hundred men girded with their weapons of war, who [are] of the sons of Dan, are standing at the opening of the gate), --
texts.jdg.18.17: yea, the five men, those going to traverse the land, go up -- they have come in thither -- they have taken the graven image, and the ephod, and the teraphim, and the molten image -- and the priest is standing at the opening of the gate, and the six hundred men who are girded with weapons of war --
texts.jdg.18.18: yea, these have entered the house of Micah, and take the graven image, the ephod, and the teraphim, and the molten image; and the priest saith unto them, `What are ye doing?'
texts.jdg.18.19: and they say to him, `Keep silent, lay thy hand on thy mouth, and go with us, and be to us for a father and for a priest: is it better thy being a priest to the house of one man, or thy being priest to a tribe and to a family in Israel?'
texts.jdg.18.20: And the heart of the priest is glad, and he taketh the ephod, and the teraphim, and the graven image, and goeth into the midst of the people,
texts.jdg.18.21: and they turn and go, and put the infants, and the cattle, and the baggage, before them.
texts.jdg.18.22: They have been far off from the house of Micah -- and the men who [are] in the houses which [are] near the house of Micah have been called together, and overtake the sons of Dan,
texts.jdg.18.23: and call unto the sons of Dan, and they turn round their faces, and say to Micah, `What -- to thee that thou hast been called together?'
texts.jdg.18.24: And he saith, `My gods which I made ye have taken, and the priest, and ye go; and what to me more? and what [is] this ye say unto me, What -- to thee!'
texts.jdg.18.25: And the sons of Dan say unto him, `Let not thy voice be heard with us, lest men bitter in soul fall upon you, and thou hast gathered thy life, and the life of thy household;'
texts.jdg.18.26: and the sons of Dan go on their way, and Micah seeth that they are stronger than he, and turneth, and goeth back unto his house.
texts.jdg.18.27: And they have taken that which Micah had made, and the priest whom he had, and come in against Laish, against a people quiet and confident, and smite them by the mouth of the sword, and the city have burnt with fire,
texts.jdg.18.28: and there is no deliverer, for it [is] far off from Zidon, and they have no word with [any] man, and it [is] in the valley which [is] by Beth-Rehob; and they build the city, and dwell in it,
texts.jdg.18.29: and call the name of the city Dan, by the name of Dan their father, who was born to Israel; and yet Laish [is] the name of the city at the first.
texts.jdg.18.30: And the sons of Dan raise up for themselves the graven image, and Jonathan son of Gershom, son of Manasseh, he and his sons have been priests to the tribe of the Danite, till the day of the removal of [the people] of the land.
texts.jdg.18.31: And they appoint for them the graven image of Micah, which he had made, all the days of the house of God being in Shiloh.
texts.jdg.19.1: And it cometh to pass, in those days, when there is no king in Israel, that there is a man a Levite, a sojourner in the sides of the hill-country of Ephraim, and he taketh to him a wife, a concubine, out of Beth-Lehem-Judah;
texts.jdg.19.2: and commit whoredom against him doth his concubine, and she goeth from him unto the house of her father, unto Beth-Lehem-Judah, and is there days -- four months.
texts.jdg.19.3: And her husband riseth and goeth after her, to speak unto her heart, to bring her back, and his young man [is] with him, and a couple of asses; and she bringeth him into the house of her father, and the father of the young woman seeth him, and rejoiceth to meet him.
texts.jdg.19.4: And keep hold on him doth his father-in-law, father of the young woman, and he abideth with him three days, and they eat and drink, and lodge there.
texts.jdg.19.5: And it cometh to pass, on the fourth day, that they rise early in the morning, and he riseth to go, and the father of the young woman saith unto his son-in-law, `Support thy heart with a morsel of bread, and afterward ye go on.'
texts.jdg.19.6: And they sit and eat both of them together, and drink, and the father of the young woman saith unto the man, `Be willing, I pray thee, and lodge all night, and let thy heart be glad.'
texts.jdg.19.7: And the man riseth to go, and his father-in-law presseth on him, and he turneth back and lodgeth there.
texts.jdg.19.8: And he riseth early in the morning, on the fifth day, to go, and the father of the young woman saith, `Support, I pray thee, thy heart;' and they have tarried till the turning of the day, and they eat, both of them.
texts.jdg.19.9: And the man riseth to go, he and his concubine, and his young man, and his father-in-law, father of the young woman, saith to him, `Lo, I pray thee, the day hath fallen toward evening, lodge all night, I pray thee; lo, the declining of the day! lodge here, and let thine heart be glad -- and ye have risen early to-morrow for your journey, and thou hast gone to thy tent.'
texts.jdg.19.10: And the man hath not been willing to lodge all night, and he riseth, and goeth, and cometh in till over-against Jebus (It [is] Jerusalem), and with him [are] a couple of asses saddled; and his concubine [is] with him.
texts.jdg.19.11: They [are] near Jebus, and the day hath gone greatly down, and the young man saith unto his lord, `Come, I pray thee, and we turn aside unto this city of the Jebusite, and lodge in it.'
texts.jdg.19.12: And his lord saith unto him, `Let us not turn aside unto the city of a stranger, that is not of the sons of Israel, thither, but we have passed over unto Gibeah.'
texts.jdg.19.13: And he saith to his young man, `Come, and we draw near to one of the places, and have lodged in Gibeah, or in Ramah.'
texts.jdg.19.14: And they pass over, and go on, and the sun goeth in upon them near Gibeah, which is to Benjamin;
texts.jdg.19.15: and they turn aside there to go in to lodge in Gibeah, and he goeth in and sitteth in a broad place of the city, and there is no man gathering them into the house to lodge.
texts.jdg.19.16: And lo, a man, an aged one, hath come from his work from the field in the evening, and the man [is] of the hill-country of Ephraim, and he [is] a sojourner in Gibeah, and the men of the place [are] Benjamites.
texts.jdg.19.17: And he lifteth up his eyes, and seeth the man, the traveller, in a broad place of the city, and the aged man saith, `Whither goest thou? and whence comest thou?'
texts.jdg.19.18: And he saith unto him, `We are passing over from Beth-Lehem-Judah unto the sides of the hill-country of Ephraim -- thence I [am], and I go unto Beth-Lehem-Judah; and to the house of Jehovah I am going, and there is no man gathering me into the house,
texts.jdg.19.19: and both straw and provender are for our asses, and also bread and wine there are for me, and for thy handmaid, and for the young man with thy servants; there is no lack of anything.'
texts.jdg.19.20: And the old man saith, `Peace to thee; only, all thy lack [is] on me, only in the broad place lodge not.'
texts.jdg.19.21: And he bringeth him in to his house, and mixeth [food] for the asses, and they wash their feet, and eat and drink.
texts.jdg.19.22: They are making their heart glad, and lo, men of the city, men -- sons of worthlessness -- have gone round about the house, beating on the door, and they speak unto the old man, the master of the house, saying, `Bring out the man who hath come unto thine house, and we know him.'
texts.jdg.19.23: And the man, the master of the house, goeth out unto them, and saith unto them, `Nay, my brethren, do not evil, I pray you, after that this man hath come in unto my house, do not this folly;
texts.jdg.19.24: lo, my daughter, the virgin, and his concubine, let me bring them out, I pray you, and humble ye them, and do to them that which is good in your eyes, and to this man do not this foolish thing.'
texts.jdg.19.25: And the men have not been willing to hearken to him, and the man taketh hold on his concubine, and bringeth [her] out unto them without, and they know her, and roll themselves upon her all the night, till the morning, and send her away in the ascending of the dawn;
texts.jdg.19.26: and the woman cometh in at the turning of the morning, and falleth at the opening of the man's house, where her lord [is], till the light.
texts.jdg.19.27: And her lord riseth in the morning, and openeth the doors of the house, and goeth out to go on his way, and lo, the woman, his concubine, is fallen at the opening of the house, and her hands [are] on the threshold,
texts.jdg.19.28: and he saith unto her, `Rise, and we go;' and there is none answering, and he taketh her on the ass, and the man riseth and goeth to his place,
texts.jdg.19.29: and cometh in unto his house, and taketh the knife, and layeth hold on his concubine, and cutteth her in pieces to her bones -- into twelve pieces, and sendeth her into all the border of Israel.
texts.jdg.19.30: And it hath come to pass, every one who seeth hath said, `There hath not been -- yea, there hath not been seen like this, from the day of the coming up of the sons of Israel out of the land of Egypt till this day; set your [heart] upon it, take counsel, and speak.'
texts.jdg.20.1: And all the sons of Israel go out, and the company is assembled as one man, from Dan even unto Beer-Sheba, and the land of Gilead, unto Jehovah, at Mizpeh.
texts.jdg.20.2: And the chiefs of all the people, of all the tribes of Israel, station themselves in the assembly of the people of God, four hundred thousand footmen drawing sword.
texts.jdg.20.3: And the sons of Benjamin hear that the sons of Israel have gone up to Mizpeh. And the sons of Israel say, `Speak ye, how hath this evil been?'
texts.jdg.20.4: And the man, the Levite, husband of the woman who hath been murdered, answereth and saith, `Into Gibeah (which [is] to Benjamin) I have come, I and my concubine, to lodge;
texts.jdg.20.5: and rise against me do the masters of Gibeah -- and they go round the house against me by night -- me they thought to slay, and my concubine they have humbled, and she dieth;
texts.jdg.20.6: and I lay hold on my concubine, and cut her in pieces, and send her into all the country of the inheritance of Israel; for they have done wickedness and folly in Israel;
texts.jdg.20.7: lo, ye [are] all sons of Israel; give for you a word and counsel here.'
texts.jdg.20.8: And all the people rise as one man, saying, `None of us doth go to his tent, and none of us doth turn aside to his house;
texts.jdg.20.9: and now, this [is] the thing which we do to Gibeah -- against it by lot!
texts.jdg.20.10: and we have taken ten men of a hundred, of all the tribes of Israel, and a hundred of a thousand, and a thousand of a myriad, to receive provision for the people, to do, at their coming to Gibeah of Benjamin, according to all the folly which it hath done in Israel.'
texts.jdg.20.11: And every man of Israel is gathered unto the city, as one man -- companions.
texts.jdg.20.12: And the tribes of Israel send men among all the tribes of Benjamin, saying, `What [is] this evil which hath been among you?
texts.jdg.20.13: And now, give up the men -- sons of worthlessness -- which [are] in Gibeah, and we put them to death, and we put away evil from Israel.' And [the sons of] Benjamin have not been willing to hearken to the voice of their brethren, the sons of Israel;
texts.jdg.20.14: and the sons of Benjamin are gathered out of the cities to Gibeah, to go out to battle with the sons of Israel.
texts.jdg.20.15: And the sons of Benjamin number themselves on that day; out of the cities [are] twenty and six thousand men drawing sword, apart from the inhabitants of Gibeah, [who] numbered themselves, seven hundred chosen men;
texts.jdg.20.16: among all this people [are] seven hundred chosen men, bound of their right hand, each of these slinging with a stone at the hair, and he doth not err.
texts.jdg.20.17: And the men of Israel numbered themselves, apart from Benjamin, four hundred thousand men, drawing sword, each of these a man of war.
texts.jdg.20.18: And they rise and go up to Beth-El, and ask of God, and the sons of Israel say, `Who doth go up for us at the commencement to battle with the sons of Benjamin?' and Jehovah saith, `Judah -- at the commencement.'
texts.jdg.20.19: And the sons of Israel rise in the morning, and encamp against Gibeah,
texts.jdg.20.20: and the men of Israel go out to battle with Benjamin, and the men of Israel set themselves in array with them, [for] battle against Gibeah,
texts.jdg.20.21: and the sons of Benjamin come out from Gibeah, and destroy in Israel on that day two and twenty thousand men -- to the earth.
texts.jdg.20.22: And the people, the men of Israel, strengthen themselves, and add to set the battle in array in the place where they arranged themselves on the first day.
texts.jdg.20.23: And the sons of Israel go up and weep before Jehovah till the evening, and ask of Jehovah, saying, `Do I add to draw nigh to battle with the sons of Benjamin, my brother?' And Jehovah saith, `Go up against him.'
texts.jdg.20.24: And the sons of Israel draw near unto the sons of Benjamin on the second day,
texts.jdg.20.25: and Benjamin cometh out to meet them from Gibeah on the second day, and destroy among the sons of Israel again eighteen thousand men -- to the earth; all these are drawing sword.
texts.jdg.20.26: And all the sons of Israel go up, even all the people, and come in to Beth-El, and weep, and sit there before Jehovah, and fast on that day till the evening, and cause to ascend burnt-offerings and peace-offerings before Jehovah.
texts.jdg.20.27: And the sons of Israel ask of Jehovah, -- and there [is] the ark of the covenant of God in those days,
texts.jdg.20.28: and Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron, is standing before it in those days -- saying, `Do I add again to go out to battle with the sons of Benjamin, my brother, or do I cease?' And Jehovah saith, `Go up, for to-morrow I give him into thy hand.'
texts.jdg.20.29: And Israel setteth liers in wait against Gibeah, round about,
texts.jdg.20.30: and the sons of Israel go up against the sons of Benjamin, on the third day, and arrange themselves against Gibeah, as time by time.
texts.jdg.20.31: And the sons of Benjamin come out to meet the people; they have been drawn away out of the city, and begin to smite [some] of the people -- wounded as time by time, in the highways (of which one is going up to Beth-El, and the other to Gibeah in the field), [are] about thirty men of Israel.
texts.jdg.20.32: And the sons of Benjamin say, `They are smitten before us as at the beginning;' but the sons of Israel said, `Let us flee, and draw them away out of the city, unto the highways.'
texts.jdg.20.33: And all the men of Israel have risen from their place, and arrange themselves at Baal-Tamar, and the ambush of Israel is coming forth out of its place, out of the meadow of Gibeah.
texts.jdg.20.34: And they come in over against Gibeah -- ten thousand chosen men out of all Israel -- and the battle [is] grievous, and they have not known that the evil is striking against them.
texts.jdg.20.35: And Jehovah smiteth Benjamin before Israel, and the sons of Israel destroy in Benjamin, on that day, twenty and five thousand, and a hundred men; all these [are] drawing sword.
texts.jdg.20.36: And the sons of Benjamin see that they have been smitten -- and the men of Israel give place to Benjamin, for they have trusted unto the ambush which they had set against Gibeah,
texts.jdg.20.37: and the ambush have hasted, and push against Gibeah, and the ambush draweth itself out, and smiteth the whole of the city by the mouth of the sword.
texts.jdg.20.38: And there was the appointed sign to the men of Israel with the ambush -- their causing to go up a great volume of smoke from the city.
texts.jdg.20.39: And the men of Israel turn in battle, and Benjamin hath begun to smite the wounded among the men of Israel, about thirty men, for they said, `Surely they are utterly smitten before us, as [at] the first battle;
texts.jdg.20.40: and the volume hath begun to go up from the city -- a pillar of smoke -- and Benjamin turneth behind, and lo, gone up hath the perfection of the city toward the heavens.
texts.jdg.20.41: And the men of Israel have turned, and the men of Benjamin are troubled, for they have seen that the evil hath stricken against them --
texts.jdg.20.42: and they turn before the men of Israel unto the way of the wilderness, and the battle hath followed them; and those who [are] from the city are destroying them in their midst;
texts.jdg.20.43: they have compassed the Benjamites -- they have pursued them -- with ease they have trodden them down till over-against Gibeah, at the sun-rising.
texts.jdg.20.44: And there fall of Benjamin eighteen thousand men -- the whole of these [are] men of valour;
texts.jdg.20.45: and they turn and flee toward the wilderness, unto the rock of Rimmon; and they glean of them in the highways five thousand men, and follow after them unto Gidom, and smite of them two thousand men.
texts.jdg.20.46: And all those falling of Benjamin are twenty and five thousand men drawing sword, on that day -- the whole of these [are] men of valour;
texts.jdg.20.47: and there turn and flee into the wilderness, unto the rock of Rimmon six hundred men, and they dwell in the rock Rimmon four months.
texts.jdg.20.48: And the men of Israel have turned back unto the sons of Benjamin, and smite them by the mouth of the sword out of the city, -- men unto cattle, unto all that is found; also all the cities which are found they have sent into fire.
texts.jdg.21.1: And the men of Israel have sworn in Mizpeh, saying, `None of us doth give his daughter to Benjamin for a wife.'
texts.jdg.21.2: And the people come in to Beth-El, and sit there till the evening before God, and lift up their voice, and weep -- a great weeping,
texts.jdg.21.3: and say, `Why, O Jehovah, God of Israel, hath this been in Israel -- to be lacking to-day, from Israel, one tribe?'
texts.jdg.21.4: And it cometh to pass on the morrow, that the people rise early, and build there an altar, and cause to ascend burnt-offerings and peace-offerings.
texts.jdg.21.5: And the sons of Israel say, `Who [is] he that hath not come up in the assembly out of all the tribes of Israel unto Jehovah?' for the great oath hath been concerning him who hath not come up unto Jehovah to Mizpeh, saying, `He is surely put to death.'
texts.jdg.21.6: And the sons of Israel repent concerning Benjamin their brother, and say, `There hath been to-day cut off one tribe from Israel,
texts.jdg.21.7: what do we do for them -- for those who are left -- for wives, and we -- we have sworn by Jehovah not to give to them of our daughters for wives?'
texts.jdg.21.8: And they say, `Who is [that] one out of the tribes of Israel who hath not come up unto Jehovah to Mizpeh?' and lo, none hath come in unto the camp from Jabesh-Gilead -- unto the assembly.
texts.jdg.21.9: And the people numbered themselves, and lo, there is not there a man of the inhabitants of Jabesh-Gilead.
texts.jdg.21.10: And the company send there twelve thousand men of the sons of valour, and command them, saying, `Go -- and ye have smitten the inhabitants of Jabesh-Gilead by the mouth of the sword, even the women and the infants.
texts.jdg.21.11: And this [is] the thing which ye do; every male, and every woman knowing the lying of a male, ye devote.'
texts.jdg.21.12: And they find out of the inhabitants of Jabesh-Gilead four hundred young women, virgins, who have not known man by the lying of a male, and they bring them in unto the camp at Shiloh, which [is] in the land of Canaan.
texts.jdg.21.13: And all the company send, and speak, unto the sons of Benjamin who [are] in the rock Rimmon, and proclaim to them peace;
texts.jdg.21.14: and Benjamin turneth back at that time, and they give to them the women whom they have kept alive of the women of Jabesh-Gilead, and they have not found for [all of] them so.
texts.jdg.21.15: And the people repented concerning Benjamin, for Jehovah had made a breach among the tribes of Israel.
texts.jdg.21.16: And the elders of the company say, `What do we do to the remnant for wives -- for the women have been destroyed out of Benjamin?'
texts.jdg.21.17: And they say, `A possession of an escaped party [is] to Benjamin, and a tribe is not blotted out from Israel;
texts.jdg.21.18: and we -- we are not able to give to them wives out of our daughters, for the sons of Israel have sworn, saying, Cursed [is] he who is giving a wife to Benjamin.'
texts.jdg.21.19: And they say, `Lo, a festival of Jehovah [is] in Shiloh, from time to time, which [is] on the north of Beth-El, at the rising of the sun, by the highway which is going up from Beth-El to Shechem, and on the south of Lebonah.'
texts.jdg.21.20: And they command the sons of Benjamin, saying, `Go -- and ye have laid wait in the vineyards,
texts.jdg.21.21: and have seen, and lo, if the daughters of Shiloh come out to dance in dances -- then ye have gone out from the vineyards, and caught for you each his wife out of the daughters of Shiloh, and gone to the land of Benjamin;
texts.jdg.21.22: and it hath been, when their fathers or their brethren come in to plead unto us, that we have said unto them, Favour us [by] them, for we have not taken [to] each his wife in battle, for ye -- ye have not given to them at this time [that] ye are guilty.'
texts.jdg.21.23: And the sons of Benjamin do so, and take women according to their number, out of the dancers whom they have taken violently away; and they go, and turn back unto their inheritance, and build the cities, and dwell in them.
texts.jdg.21.24: And the sons of Israel go up and down thence at that time, each to his tribe, and to his family; and they go out thence each to his inheritance.
texts.jdg.21.25: In those days there is no king in Israel; each doth that which is right in his own eyes.

texts.jdg.1.1: Y aconteció después de la muerte de Josué, que los hijos de Israel consultaron a Jehová, diciendo: ¿Quién subirá por nosotros el primero a pelear contra los Cananeos?
texts.jdg.1.2: Y Jehová respondió: Judá subirá: he aquí que yo he entregado la tierra en sus manos.
texts.jdg.1.3: Y Judá dijo a Simeón su hermano: Sube conmigo en mi suerte y peleemos contra el Cananeo: y yo también iré contigo en tu suerte. Y Simeón fue con él.
texts.jdg.1.4: Y subió Judá, y Jehová entregó en sus manos al Cananeo, y al Ferezeo: e hirieron de ellos en Bezec diez mil hombres.
texts.jdg.1.5: Y hallaron a Adoni-bezec en Bezec, y pelearon contra él: e hirieron al Cananeo, y al Ferezeo.
texts.jdg.1.6: Mas Adoni-bezec huyó: y siguiéronle, y prendiéronle, y cortáronle los pulgares de las manos y de los pies.
texts.jdg.1.7: Entonces dijo Adoni-bezec: Setenta reyes cortados los pulgares de sus manos y de sus pies cogían las migajas debajo de mi mesa: como yo hice, así me ha pagado Dios. Y metiéronle en Jerusalem, donde murió.
texts.jdg.1.8: Y habían combatido los hijos de Judá a Jerusalem, y la habían tomado, y pasado a cuchillo, y puesto a fuego la ciudad:
texts.jdg.1.9: Después los hijos de Judá descendieron para pelear contra el Cananeo, que habitaba en las montañas, y al mediodía, y en los llanos.
texts.jdg.1.10: Y partió Judá contra el Cananeo, que habitaba en Hebrón, la cual se llamaba antes Cariat-arbe, e hirieron a Sesai, a Ahimán, y a Tolmai.
texts.jdg.1.11: Y de allí fue a los que habitaban en Dabir, que antes se llamaba Cariat-sefer.
texts.jdg.1.12: Y dijo Caleb: El que hiriere a Cariat-sefer, y la tomáre yo le daré a Aja mi hija por mujer.
texts.jdg.1.13: Y tomóla Otoniel, hijo de Cenez, hermano de Caleb menor que él: y él le dio a Aja su hija por mujer.
texts.jdg.1.14: Y cuando la llevaban, persuadióle que pidiese a su padre tierras para labrar. Y ella descendió del asno: y Caleb le dijo: ¿Qué tienes?
texts.jdg.1.15: Ella entonces le respondió: Dáme una bendición: que pues me has dado tierra de secadal me des también fuentes de aguas. Entonces Caleb le dio las fuentes de arriba, y las fuentes de abajo.
texts.jdg.1.16: Y los hijos del Cineo suegro de Moisés subieron de la ciudad de las palmas con los hijos de Judá al desierto de Judá, que es al mediodía de Arad: y fueron y habitaron con el pueblo.
texts.jdg.1.17: Judá pues fue a su hermano Simeón, e hirieron al Cananeo que habitaba en Sefat, y asoláronla: y pusieron por nombre a la ciudad, Jorma.
texts.jdg.1.18: Tomó también Judá a Gaza con su término: y a Ascalón con su término: y a Accarón con su término.
texts.jdg.1.19: Y fue Jehová con Judá, y echó a los de las montañas: mas no pudo echar a los que habitaban en las campañas, los cuales tenían carros herrados.
texts.jdg.1.20: Y dieron a Caleb a Hebrón, como Moisés había dicho: él cual echó de allí a tres hijos de Enac.
texts.jdg.1.21: ¶ Mas al Jebuseo, que habitaba en Jerusalem no echaron los hijos de Ben-jamín, antes el Jebuseo habitó con los hijos de Ben-jamín en Jerusalem hasta hoy.
texts.jdg.1.22: ¶ También los de la casa de José subieron a Bet-el: y fue Jehová con ellos.
texts.jdg.1.23: Y los de la casa de José pusieron espías en Bet-el, la cual ciudad antes se llamaba Luza.
texts.jdg.1.24: Y los que espiaban, vieron un hombre que salía de la ciudad, y dijéronle: Muéstranos ahora la entrada de la ciudad, y haremos contigo misericordia.
texts.jdg.1.25: Y él les mostró la entrada a la ciudad, e hiriéronla a filo de espada, y dejaron a aquel hombre con toda su parentela.
texts.jdg.1.26: Y aquel hombre se fue a la tierra de los Jetteos, y edificó una ciudad, a la cual llamó Luza: y este es su nombre hasta hoy.
texts.jdg.1.27: Tampoco Manasés echó a los de Bet-sán, ni a los de sus aldeas: ni a los de Tanac, y sus aldeas: ni a los que habitaban en Jeblaam, y en sus aldeas: ni a los que habitaban en Mageddo y en sus aldeas: mas el Cananeo quiso habitar en esta tierra.
texts.jdg.1.28: Mas cuando Israel tomó fuerzas, hizo al Cananeo tributario: pero no le echó.
texts.jdg.1.29: Tampoco Efraím echó al Cananeo que habitaba en Gazer, antes habito el Cananeo en medio de él en Gazer.
texts.jdg.1.30: Tampoco Zabulón echó los que habitaban en Cetrón, y a los que habitaban en Naalol: mas el Cananeo habitó en medio de él, y le fueron tributarios.
texts.jdg.1.31: Tampoco Aser echó a los que habitaban en Acob, y a los que habitaban en Sidón, y en Acalab, y en Acasib, y en Helba, y en Afed, y en Rohob:
texts.jdg.1.32: Antes moró Aser entre los Cananeos, que habitaban en la tierra, que no los echó.
texts.jdg.1.33: Tampoco Neftalí echó los que habitaban en Bet-semes, y a los que habitaban en Bet-avat: mas moró entre los Cananeos, que habitaban en la tierra: mas fuéronle tributarios los moradores de Bet-semes, y los moradores de Bet-avat.
texts.jdg.1.34: Los Amorreos apretaron a los hijos de Dan hasta el monte, que no los dejaron descender a la campaña:
texts.jdg.1.35: Y el Amorreo quiso habitar en el monte de Hares, en Ajalón, y en Salebim; mas como la mano de la casa de José tomó fuerzas, hiciéronlos tributarios.
texts.jdg.1.36: Y el término del Amorreo fue desde la subida de Acrabim, y desde la piedra, y arriba.
texts.jdg.2.1: Y el ángel de Jehová subió de Galgala a Boquim, y dijo: Yo os saqué de Egipto, y os metí en la tierra de la cual había jurado a vuestros padres; y dije: No invalidaré mi concierto con vosotros para siempre:
texts.jdg.2.2: Con tal que vosotros no hagáis alianza con los moradores de aquesta tierra, antes destruiréis sus altares: mas vosotros no habéis oído mi voz. ¿Por qué lo habéis hecho?
texts.jdg.2.3: Y yo también dije: No los echaré de delante de vosotros: y seros han por azote para vuestros costados, y sus dioses por tropezadero.
texts.jdg.2.4: Y como el ángel de Jehová habló estas palabras a todos los hijos de Israel, el pueblo lloró a alta voz.
texts.jdg.2.5: Y llamaron por nombre a aquel lugar Boquim: y sacrificáron allí a Jehová.
texts.jdg.2.6: ¶ Porque ya Josué había enviado el pueblo, y los hijos de Israel se habían ido cada uno a su herencia para poseerla.
texts.jdg.2.7: Y el pueblo había servido a Jehová todo el tiempo de Josué, y todo el tiempo de los ancianos que vivieron largos días después de Josué: que habían visto todas las grandes obras de Jehová, que había hecho con Israel.
texts.jdg.2.8: Y murió Josué hijo de Nun, siervo de Jehová, siendo de ciento y diez años,
texts.jdg.2.9: Y enterráronle en el término de su heredad en Tamnat-sare, en el monte de Efraím, al norte del monte de Gaas.
texts.jdg.2.10: Y toda aquella generación también fue recogida con sus padres: y levantóse después de ellos otra generación, que no conocían a Jehová, ni a la obra que él había hecho a Israel.
texts.jdg.2.11: Y los hijos de Israel hicieron lo malo en ojos de Jehová, y sirvieron a los Baales.
texts.jdg.2.12: Y dejaron a Jehová el Dios de sus padres, que los había sacado de la tierra de Egipto, y fuéronse tras otros dioses, tras los dioses de los pueblos que estaban en sus al derredores, a los cuales adoraron, y provocaron a ira a Jehová.
texts.jdg.2.13: Y dejaron a Jehová, y adoraron a Baal y a Astarot.
texts.jdg.2.14: Y el furor de Jehová se encendió contra Israel, el cual los entregó en manos de robadores, que los robaron: y los vendió en manos de sus enemigos, que estaban en sus al derredores: y nunca más pudieron parar delante de sus enemigos.
texts.jdg.2.15: Por donde quiera que salían, la mano de Jehová era contra ellos en mal, como había dicho Jehová: y como Jehová se lo había jurado, así los afligió en gran manera.
texts.jdg.2.16: Mas Jehová despertó jueces, que los librasen de mano de los que los saqueaban:
texts.jdg.2.17: Mas tampoco oyeron a sus jueces, antes fornicaron tras dioses ajenos, a los cuales adoraron: y se apartaron presto del camino en que anduvieron sus padres obedeciendo a los mandamientos de Jehová: mas ellos no hicieron así.
texts.jdg.2.18: Y cuando les despertaba Jehová jueces, Jehová era con el juez, y librábalos de mano de los enemigos todo el tiempo de aquel juez: porque Jehová se arrepentía por su gemido a causa de los que los oprimían y afligían.
texts.jdg.2.19: Mas en muriendo el juez, ellos se tornaban, y se corrompían más que sus padres siguiendo dioses ajenos, sirviéndoles y encorvándose delante de ellos: y nada disminuían de sus obras, y de su camino duro.
texts.jdg.2.20: ¶ Y la ira de Jehová se encendió contra Israel, y dijo: Pues que esta gente traspasa mi concierto que mandé a sus padres, y no obedecen mi voz;
texts.jdg.2.21: Tampoco yo echaré más delante de ellos a nadie de aquestas gentes, que dejó Josué cuando murió:
texts.jdg.2.22: Para que por ellas yo probase a Israel, si ellos guardarían el camino de Jehová, andando por él, como sus padres lo guardaron, o no.
texts.jdg.2.23: Por tanto, Jehová dejó aquellas gentes, y no las desarraigó luego, ni las entregó en mano de Josué.
texts.jdg.3.1: Estas pues son las gentes que dejó Jehová para probar con ellas a Israel, es a saber, a todos los que no habían conocido todas las guerras de Canaán.
texts.jdg.3.2: Solamente las dejó para que el linaje de los hijos de Israel conociese, y para enseñarlos en la guerra, a aquellos solamente que antes no la habían conocido.
texts.jdg.3.3: Cinco príncipes de los Filisteos, y todos los Cananeos, y los Sidonios, y los Heveos que habitaban en el monte Líbano desde el monte de Baal-hermón hasta llegar a Emat.
texts.jdg.3.4: Estos pues fueron dejados para probar por ellos a Israel, para saber, si obedecían a los mandamientos de Jehová, que había mandado a sus padres por mano de Moisés.
texts.jdg.3.5: Y como los hijos de Israel habitaban entre los Cananeos, Jetteos, Amorreos, Ferezeos, Heveos, y Jebuseos:
texts.jdg.3.6: Tomaron de sus hijas por mujeres, y dieron sus hijas a los hijos de ellos, y sirvieron a sus dioses.
texts.jdg.3.7: E hicieron lo malo los hijos de Israel en ojos de Jehová: y olvidados de Jehová su Dios sirvieron a los Baales, y a los (ídolos de los) bosques.
texts.jdg.3.8: Y la saña de Jehová se encendió contra Israel, y vendióles en manos de Cusan-rasataim rey de Mesopotamia, y sirvieron los hijos de Israel a Cusan-rasataim ocho años.
texts.jdg.3.9: ¶ Y clamaron los hijos de Israel a Jehová, y Jehová despertó salvador a los hijos de Israel, y librólos, es a saber, a Otoniel hijo de Cenez, hermano menor de Caleb.
texts.jdg.3.10: Y el Espíritu de Jehová fue sobre él, y juzgó a Israel, y salió en batalla, y Jehová entregó en su mano a Cusan-rasataim rey de Siria: y prevaleció su mano contra Cusan-rasataim.
texts.jdg.3.11: Y reposó la tierra cuarenta años: y murió Otoniel hijo de Cenez.
texts.jdg.3.12: ¶ Y tornaron los hijos de Israel a hacer lo malo delante de los ojos de Jehová: y Jehová esforzó a Eglón rey de Moab contra Israel, por cuanto habían hecho lo malo delante de los ojos de Jehová.
texts.jdg.3.13: Y juntó consigo a los hijos de Ammón, y de Amalec; y fue, e hirió a Israel, y tomó la ciudad de las palmas.
texts.jdg.3.14: Y sirvieron los hijos de Israel a Eglón rey de los Moabitas diez y ocho años.
texts.jdg.3.15: Y clamaron los hijos de Israel a Jehová, y Jehová les despertó salvador, a Aod, hijo de Gera, hijo de Jemini, el cual tenía cerrada la mano derecha. Y los hijos de Israel enviaron con él un presente a Eglón rey de Moab.
texts.jdg.3.16: Y Aod se había hecho un cuchillo agudo de ambas partes de longura de un codo: y traíalo ceñido debajo de sus vestidos a su lado derecho.
texts.jdg.3.17: Y presentó el presente a Eglón rey de Moab: y Eglón era hombre muy grueso:
texts.jdg.3.18: Y luego que él hubo presentado el presente, envió al pueblo que habían traído el presente.
texts.jdg.3.19: Y tornándose desde los ídolos que están en Galgala, dijo: Rey, una palabra secreta tengo que decirte. El entonces dijo: Calla. Y saliéronse de delante de él todos los que estaban delante de él.
texts.jdg.3.20: Y Aod entró a él, el cual estaba sentado solo en una sala de verano. Y Aod dijo: Tengo palabra de Dios para ti. El entonces se levantó de la silla.
texts.jdg.3.21: Mas Aod metió su mano izquierda, y tomó el cuchillo de su lado derecho, y metióselo por el vientre,
texts.jdg.3.22: De tal manera que la empuñadura entró también tras la hoja, y la grosura encerró la hoja, que él no sacó el cuchillo de su vientre: y el estiércol salió.
texts.jdg.3.23: Y saliendo Aod al patio cerró tras sí las puertas de la sala.
texts.jdg.3.24: Y salido él, vinieron sus siervos, los cuales viendo las puertas de la sala cerradas, dijeron: sin duda él cubre sus pies en la sala de verano.
texts.jdg.3.25: Y habiendo esperado hasta estar confusos, que él no abría las puertas de la sala, tomaron la llave, y abrieron. Y, he aquí, su señor caído en tierra muerto.
texts.jdg.3.26: Mas entre tanto que ellos se detuvieron, Aod se escapó, y pasando los ídolos salvóse en Seirat.
texts.jdg.3.27: Y en entrando, toca el cuerno en el monte de Efraím, y los hijos de Israel descendieron con él del monte, y él iba delante de ellos.
texts.jdg.3.28: Entonces él les dijo: Seguídme, porque Jehová ha entregado vuestros enemigos los Moabitas en vuestras manos. Y descendieron en pos de él, y tomaron los vados del Jordán a Moab; y no dejaron pasar a ninguno.
texts.jdg.3.29: E hirieron en aquel tiempo de los Moabitas como diez mil hombres, todos valientes, y todos hombres de guerra: no escapó varón.
texts.jdg.3.30: Y Moab fue sujetado aquel día debajo de la mano de Israel: y reposó la tierra ochenta años.
texts.jdg.3.31: Después de este, fue Samgar hijo de Anat, el cual hirió seiscientos hombres de los Filisteos con una aguijada de los bueyes; y él también salvó a Israel.
texts.jdg.4.1: Mas los hijos de Israel tornaron a hacer lo malo en los ojos de Jehová, después de la muerte de Aod.
texts.jdg.4.2: Y Jehová los vendió en mano de Jabín rey de Canaán, el cual reinó en Asor: y el capitán de su ejército se llamaba Sísera, y él habitaba en Haroset de las gentes.
texts.jdg.4.3: Y los hijos de Israel clamaron a Jehová; porque aquel tenía nuevecientos carros herrados; y había afligido en gran manera a los hijos de Israel por veinte años.
texts.jdg.4.4: Y gobernaba en aquel tiempo a Israel una mujer, Débora profetisa, mujer de Lapidot.
texts.jdg.4.5: La cual Débora habitaba debajo de una palma entre Rama y Bet-el, en el monte de Efraím: y los hijos de Israel subían a ella a juicio.
texts.jdg.4.6: Y ella envió a llamar a Barac hijo de Abinoem de Cedes de Neftalí, y díjole: ¿No te ha mandado Jehová Dios de Israel, diciendo: Vé, y haz gente en el monte de Tabor; y toma contigo diez mil hombres de los hijos de Neftalí, y de los hijos de Zabulón?
texts.jdg.4.7: Y yo atraeré a ti al arroyo de Cisón a Sísera capitán del ejército de Jabín, con sus carros y su ejército, y entregártelo he en tus manos.
texts.jdg.4.8: Y Barac le respondió: Si tú fueres conmigo, yo iré; y si no fueres conmigo, no iré.
texts.jdg.4.9: Y ella dijo: Yo iré contigo, mas no será tu honra en el camino que vas, porque en mano de mujer venderá Jehová a Sísera. Y levantándose Débora vino con Barac a Cedes.
texts.jdg.4.10: Y juntó Barac a Zabulón y Neftalí en Cedes, y subió con diez mil hombres de a pie; y Débora subió con él.
texts.jdg.4.11: Y Jeber Cineo de los hijos de Hobab suegro de Moisés, se había apartado de los Cineos, y había puesto su tienda hasta el valle de Sennim, que es junto a Cedes.
texts.jdg.4.12: Vinieron pues las nuevas a Sísera como Barac hijo de Abinoem había subido al monte de Tabor.
texts.jdg.4.13: Y juntó Sísera todos sus carros, nuevecientos carros herrados con todo el pueblo que estaba con él desde Haroset de las gentes hasta el arroyo de Cisón.
texts.jdg.4.14: Entonces Débora dijo a Barac: Levántate; porque este es el día en que Jehová ha entregado a Sísera en tus manos. ¿No ha salido Jehová delante de ti? Y Barac descendió del monte de Tabor, y diez mil hombres en pos de él.
texts.jdg.4.15: Y Jehová quebrantó a Sísera, y a todos sus carros, y a todo su ejército a filo de espada delante de Barac: y Sísera descendió del carro, y huyo a pie.
texts.jdg.4.16: Mas Barac siguió los carros y el ejército hasta Haroset de las gentes, y todo el ejército de Sísera cayó a filo de espada, hasta no quedar ni uno.
texts.jdg.4.17: ¶ Y Sísera se acogió a pie a la tienda de Jahel mujer de Jeber Cineo; porque había paz entre Jabín rey de Asor, y la casa de Jeber Cineo.
texts.jdg.4.18: Y saliendo Jahel a recibir a Sísera, díjole: Ven señor mío, ven a mí, no hayas temor. Y él vino a ella a la tienda; y ella le cubrió con una manta.
texts.jdg.4.19: Y él le dijo: Dáme a beber ahora una poca de agua, que tengo sed. Y ella abrió un cuero de leche, y dióle de beber, y tornóle a cubrir.
texts.jdg.4.20: Y él la dijo: Estáte a la puerta de la tienda, y si alguno viniere, y te preguntare, diciendo: ¿Hay aquí alguno? tú responderás que no.
texts.jdg.4.21: Y Jahel la mujer de Jeber tomó la estaca de la tienda, y poniendo un mazo en su mano, vino a él calladamente, y metióle la estaca por las sienes, y enclavóle con la tierra: y él estaba cargado del sueño y cansado, y así murió.
texts.jdg.4.22: Y siguiendo Barac a Sísera, Jahel le salió a recibir, y díjole: Ven, y mostrarte he al varón, que tú buscas; y él entró donde ella estaba, y, he aquí, Sísera estaba tendido muerto, la estaca atravesada por la sien.
texts.jdg.4.23: Y aquel día sujeto Dios a Jabín rey de Canaán delante de los hijos de Israel.
texts.jdg.4.24: Y la mano de los hijos de Israel comenzó a crecer, y a fortificarse contra Jabín rey de Canaán hasta que le destruyeron.
texts.jdg.5.1: Y aquel día cantó Débora y Barac hijo de Abinoem, diciendo:
texts.jdg.5.2: Porque ha vengado las injurias de Israel, porque el pueblo se ha ofrecido de su voluntad, load a Jehová.
texts.jdg.5.3: Oíd reyes: estád atentos príncipes, yo cantaré a Jehová: diré salmos a Jehová Dios de Israel.
texts.jdg.5.4: Cuando saliste de Seir, oh Jehová, cuando te apartaste del campo de Edom, la tierra tembló, y los cielos destilaron, y las nubes gotearon aguas.
texts.jdg.5.5: Los montes se derritieron delante de Jehová, este Sinaí, delante de Jehová Dios de Israel.
texts.jdg.5.6: En los días de Samgar hijo de Anat, en los días de Jahel cesaron los caminos; y los que andaban por las sendas, se apartaban por sendas torcidas.
texts.jdg.5.7: Las aldeas habían cesado en Israel, habían cesado: hasta que yo Débora me levanté, me levanté madre en Israel.
texts.jdg.5.8: En escogiendo nuevos dioses, la guerra estaba a las puertas: ¿Se veía escudo o lanza entre cuarenta mil en Israel?
texts.jdg.5.9: Mi corazón es a los príncipes de Israel, a los voluntarios en el pueblo, load a Jehová.
texts.jdg.5.10: Los que cabalgáis en asnas blancas, los que presidís en juicio, y los que andáis por el camino, hablád.
texts.jdg.5.11: A causa del estruendo de los flecheros quitado de entre los que sacan las aguas: allí recuenten las justicias de Jehová, las justicias de sus aldeas en Israel. Ahora el pueblo de Jehová descenderá a las puertas.
texts.jdg.5.12: Despierta, despierta Débora, despierta, despierta, di canción. Levántate Barac, y lleva tus cautivos, hijo de Abinoem.
texts.jdg.5.13: Entonces ha hecho que el que quedó del pueblo; señoree los magníficos: Jehová me hizo enseñorear sobre los fuertes.
texts.jdg.5.14: De Efraím salió su raíz contra Amalec: tras ti vino Ben-jamín contra tus pueblos. De Maquir descendieron príncipes: y de Zabulón los que solían tratar cincel de escriba.
texts.jdg.5.15: Príncipes también de Isacar fueron con Débora: y también Isacar, como Barac, se puso a pie en el valle: de las divisiones de Rubén son grandes las disputas del corazón.
texts.jdg.5.16: ¿Por qué te quedaste entre las majadas, para oír los silvos de los rebaños? De las divisiones de Rubén grandes son las disputas del corazón.
